key_insight: The paper introduces an automated way to estimate floating-point rounding error inside finite element kernels while the kernel computes its value, helping catch accuracy loss before it breaks a simulation.
engineering_relevance: This makes FEM code more reliable for nonlinear mechanics, ill-conditioned meshes, reduced-precision workflows, and kernel debugging in production solvers.
method: Wrap kernel arithmetic in a custom type that carries both value and running forward-error estimate.
Integrate the approach into the FEniCS Form Compiler (FFCx) via a C++ backend that generates type-generic templated kernels.
Use Running Error Analysis (REA) to compute an a posteriori error bound concurrently with each finite element operation.
evidence_signal: The authors validate the framework on a Neo-Hooke hyperelasticity cancellation case and a near-degenerate Laplace assembly, reporting typical runtime overhead of only about 2–4x.
watch_item: The approach adds overhead and depends on kernel-generation integration, so it may need careful tuning for large-scale or performance-critical HPC workflows.
paper_title: Running error bounds in finite element kernels
